insight.title: Why Putting Things Out of Reach Helps You Decide
insight.subtitle: How physical space helps you make better choices without trying

sections.text: Your brain treats physical proximity as a command, not a suggestion. If an item is within your immediate reach, you aren’t really deciding to use it—you are simply reacting to its physical closeness.

Space acts as a natural filter for intent. By adding just a few feet of distance, you force your brain to switch from instinctive grabbing to deliberate evaluating. It is an effortless mental guardrail.
Whether it is a phone or a distraction, physical distance defines your discipline. When you control the space around you, you stop fighting your impulses and start removing their power entirely.
Try this today: When you make a decision today, take one step back from what you are looking at.
Your environment is either a trap for your impulses or a stage for your intentions.
